newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers up sharply, thin trade except France.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers up sharply, thin trade except France.

text.p: ARA bunkers rose sharply, in a thin market in which only southern French ports managed end-of-week trade, dealers said.

Rotterdam 380 cst fuel oil rose to $123 fob by mid-afternoon, as barge prices raced to five-year highs, but had softened by the session close to $121/$122. Dealers said demand on Wednesday and Thursday was reasonable, but postponements had pushed sales forward from mid-week to Friday to next week.
Dealers said even enquiries were low on Friday.
Hamburg prices rose sharply in line with ARA increases, deterring almost all buyers.
"We're following Rotterdam unfortunately and no one wants to buy," one supplier said.

Mediterranean prices were generally firmer on Friday, except for southern France where they were steady. The stability drew a number of buyers into Fos, one of the cheapest Mediterranean bunkering ports.
"We've really been quite busy today. Buyers were hoping for price falls. They didn't get them and just accepted they had no choice," one supplier said.
Durban prices were steady, with no supply problems and stocks restored to healthy levels.
